recipes.name: Top Shelf Margaritas on the Rocks

steps.text: Make a simple syrup by stirring together and bringing 2/3 cup sugar and 1/3 cup water to a boil until the sugar dissolves; set aside to cool.
Make the sour mix by briskly stirring together the 2 1/4 cups water, lemon juice, 1/4 cup sugar, and egg white; set aside.
Combine the ice cubes, tequila, Cointreau, lime juice, 1 ounce of the simple syrup, and 1/2 cup of the sour mix in a pitcher; stir vigorously to infuse the ice, 8 to 15 seconds.

Run a lime wedge along the rim of an 8-ounce glass. Spread the kosher salt onto a plate and dip the glass rims in the salt to coat; add ice if desired. Strain the mixture from the cocktail shaker into the glass to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Top Shelf Margaritas on the Rocks
raw_recipe.description: Top Shelf Margaritas sure to please the avid 'rita fanatic; as with anything, fresh ingredients are the key to a quality result, so we start with our own syrup and sour mix.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe. Although I used splenda (2 Tbsp) instead of the simple syrup and I do not add the egg. They are great and friends love the fact that it is lower cal.

These were really good. I made a double batch and it fit perfectly in my pitcher without any ice. I didn't want to water down the cocktail so instead of adding ice in the pitcher I just shook each one with ice in a shaker before serving in a salt-rimmed glass. I only made half of the sour mix and had plenty for the double batch with some left over. I also had leftover simple syrup but I wanted that just to have in my fridge. Like other reviewers said, its a strong drink but delicious with the fresh ingredients. You can add more or less alcohol or simple syrup to your liking
Doubled the recipe , left out the egg whites, and served at a party. Added 50% more simple syrup. We used 100% Agave Tequila. Margaritas were a big hit.

My first time making a margarita. Yummy. I used lime juice in the sour mix since that's all I had, and I nixed the egg white. My only complaint is that the recipe makes odd amounts of simple syrup and sour mix...

Wow I just realized when I came to rate this that I made them wrong. I made as directed, without the egg white (Seemed kinda odd to me), and by mistake I did not add that last 1/2 cup of lime juice. I don't know why... I didn't even see it in the ingredients somehow! I did use a mixture of lemons and limes in the sour mix though, and it was slightly more than the 1/ 1/2 cups. I poured all of that into the pitcher. It's weird the recipe tells you to make all that sour mix and not use it all... But the end result were very good margaritas that are not too sweet. I used only 1 1/2 cups tequila instead of 2 cups, and although I would have preferred them full strength, all my guests still thought they were pretty strong and were glad I didn't use anymore tequila than that. I also kept the remaining simple syrup and let people add some if they preferred a sweeter taste.

Wow. Yum! I made the recipe to take to a Cooking Light supper club tonight, and it's a very authentic-tasting margarita! It's a fair amount of work, juicing all the lemons & limes, but the final taste is worth it for sure. I rated the recipe a '4' because I used 1/2 the amount of tequila (using the whole amount would have been waaaaay too much, for me). I also omitted the egg white; although I'm not too squeamish about raw egg myself, I'm bringing it to serve to a group. Plus, I want to use the leftover sour mix to make lemonade for my kids. Thanks for the recipe!!
This was awesome! Don’t leave out the egg. The acidity in the lemon and lime juice will eliminate any bacteria you may be worried about. These were a big hit!
Yum Mo! Followed recipe to a T. It was the perfect cocktail to go with steak & chicken fajitas.

Short and sweet... I've made these numerous times (using all the sour mix and simple syrup recipe calls for) and every time I've been told they were the best margarita's they'd ever had. The issue is that they taste so good that people don't realize how much alcohol they are drinking, so watch out for that!

Exceptional! We're not drinkers, but enjoy an occasional Margarita with some great mexican food. These are wonderful. Squeezed fresh limes and lemons, made exactly as recipe called for...perfect! mmmmmm....don't forget to salt the rims!

Excellent. I'm was a bit worried about the raw egg but decided to live on the edge... This recipe ROCKS!! (NO pun intended! tee-hee). Scaled it down to 4. There's just two of us tonight. No need for 16 margaritas between the two of us. LOL - Wouldn't that prove for a great evening?

The recipe as is has too much alcohol in it for me, so I lightened it up with more juice. Good recipe. Thanks.
Fresh ingredients make all the difference!!! Excellent recipe.
It is very tasty and doesn't have that artificial-ness as the bottled "fake" sour mixes bring but this was MUCHO STRONG!!!!
